html:
The British American colonies on the map in 1715 are the English colonies of the Atlantic coast of North America, from Carolina to Maine, which became the Thirteen Colonies.

They began with Jamestown in Virginia in 1607 and Plymouth in 1620, followed by Massachusetts Bay in 1630 and many others. New York was taken from the Dutch as New Amsterdam in 1664, Carolina was settled from 1670 and Pennsylvania from 1681. Georgia, the last of the thirteen, came only in 1732.

The colonies differed a great deal. New England was a land of Puritan farms, towns and fishing, born of the Puritan migration. The Chesapeake and Carolina grew tobacco and rice with enslaved Africans brought by the Atlantic slave trade. Each colony had its own assembly, and they grew fast: from about 250,000 people in 1700 to well over two million by the 1770s.

In 1715 Carolina was fighting the Yamasee War, one of many wars with Native nations as settlement pushed inland. After Britain tried to tax them in the 1760s, the colonies rebelled and declared independence in 1776 as the United States. See British North America for the chart.
